NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay broke with a long-standing assembly convention on Thursday when he left his designated chair and took a seat alongside ministers in the front row during the afternoon session. It was unusual for a chief minister to occupy a seat meant for ministers, news agency PTI reported citing a source.Vijay, who normally sits in a separate chair positioned close to Speaker J C D Prabhakar, moved across the front row and sat between ministers K A Sengottaiyan, who is also the leader of the House, and Aadhav Arjuna.The move drew attention as chief ministers traditionally occupy a separate designated seat in the House, while ministers sit alongside them according to seniority.Members of the House occasionally change seats briefly to interact with colleagues. However, Vijay's move was notable because he shifted from his official chair and remained seated among the ministers.The chief minister had attended government programmes earlier in the day and arrived at the assembly for the later session.The 234-member Tamil Nadu assembly follows a conventional seating arrangement in which the chief minister occupies a designated chair near the Speaker, while ministers are seated separately in the front row.The opposition leaders sit across from the treasury benches, with their respective party members seated behind them.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay broke with a long-standing assembly convention. He left his designated chair and took a seat alongside ministers in the front row. It was unusual for a chief minister to occupy a seat meant for ministers.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Thursday questioned what he described as conflicting statements by senior military officials on the extent of cooperation between Pakistan and China during Operation Sindoor Sharing video clips on X, Ramesh said Deputy Chief of Army Staff Lt Gen Rahul Singh had, on July 4, 2025, highlighted what he called the “very disturbingly deep nature” of the Pakistan-China partnership during the military operation.The Congress leader contrasted those remarks with comments made by former Chief of Defence Staff Gen. The nation is confused," said Ramesh on X.The Congress leader questioned whether the differing accounts reflected a broader effort to shape the public narrative around India's relations with China.“What is going on here? Is there some deeper plan to change the narrative?” he asked.He also linked the issue to the Centre's broader China policy, alleging that there had been a “calibrated capitulation to China” and citing what he described as the Prime Minister's “infamous clean chit to China on June 2020” as well as India's record trade deficits with China.Ramesh's remarks came ex-CDS Chauhan, speaking at the ‘VIMARSH’ event on Operation Sindoor and its aftermath at the Vivekananda International Foundation, said Pakistan had failed to obtain evidence of the targets struck by India despite attempts to access commercial satellite imagery.Chauhan said the presence of Chinese personnel supporting Pakistan's military equipment during Operation Sindoor should be viewed in the context of "contractual obligations", while cautioning against drawing conclusions beyond established facts.In the clip shared by Ramesh, General Singh can be heard stating that the key lessons from Operation Sindoor were that India faced a multi-adversary challenge, with Pakistan at the forefront and China and Turkey providing significant military support. He added that China also used the conflict to assess its weapons and systems in a real-world environment.India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7, 2025, days after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people. The operation targeted terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK).

NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Thursday met representatives of Reservation Hatao Andolan, which is protesting against caste-based reservation and demanding a complete overhaul at the national capital's Jantar Mantar.In a social media post on X, Nadda said that he met Harsh Dubey, Mrityunjay Pathak and Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan as per the pre-determined schedule, adding that another meeting will be held soon."Following the movement that took place at Jantar Mantar on August 21, cordial discussions were held, as per the pre-determined schedule, with Shri Harsh Dubey, Shri Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan, and Shri Mrityunjay Pathak, members of the team. Article Title: Delhi HC quashes criminal defamation case against senior advocate Pinaki Misra
Article Text:
The Delhi High Court has quashed criminal defamation proceedings against senior advocate and former Member of Parliament Pinaki Misra

New Delhi: The Delhi High Court has quashed criminal defamation proceedings against senior advocate and former Member of Parliament Pinaki Misra, in a case alleging that he had said certain objectionable words about a lawyer in an interview.The high court also quashed a trial court's April 2019 order summoning Misra to face trial for defamation, saying permitting the proceedings to continue would not advance the cause of justice.Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said the complainant had examined himself as the sole witness and had not provided any material to prima facie demonstrate that the alleged imputation had lowered his reputation in others' estimation."There is no material on record, in the form of statement of any other person or otherwise, to prima facie demonstrate that the alleged imputation had the effect of lowering the reputation of Respondent No 2 (complainant) in the estimation of others."The allegation that the publication caused damage to his reputation, by itself, remains an assertion of the complainant and does not establish the statutory requirement contemplated by Explanation 4 to Section 499 (defamation) of IPC," the court said in its order passed on August 25.The high court said permitting the criminal proceedings to continue would not advance the cause of justice and instead subject the petitioner (Misra) to the rigours of a criminal trial in the absence of sufficient foundational material."Accordingly, this court deems it appropriate, in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 482 of CrPC, to quash the impugned summoning order and the consequential proceedings arising therefrom. The petition is accordingly allowed," it said.It was alleged that the complainant advocate had filed a complaint with the Bar Council of Delhi in 2018 against Misra, alleging that the senior advocate's appearance on behalf of power distribution companies before the National Green Tribunal amounted to professional misconduct.After the dispute was reported in a newspaper, it was alleged that Misra gave an interview to another newspaper in which he purportedly used certain objectionable words against the complainant.The complainant filed two defamation complaints alleging that Misra's objectionable remarks have lowered his reputation in the eyes of the public and also affected his professional life.The high court, in its order, noted that the allegation against Misra was founded upon the contents of an online news report.It said Misra had specifically denied having given the interview and had communicated in March 2019 to the editor of the news establishment, denying that he gave the alleged interview and seeking the publication's clarification.The court said the alleged imputation was founded upon an online news report, which has not been supported by examination of the concerned reporter, author, editor or any other person associated with the news portal, particularly when the petitioner had specifically denied having made the alleged statement and had also sent a communication seeking clarification in this regard.PTI
Article Summary: Delhi High Court quashes criminal defamation proceedings against Pinaki Misra. Case alleged he had said certain objectionable words about a lawyer in an interview. High court also quashed a trial court's April 2019 order summoning Misra to face trial for defamation.

Article Title: 'Took off for Kathmandu blissfully unaware': Shashi Tharoor on deadly Nepal floods
Article Text:
Tharoor said he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Thursday said that he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district when he left for Kathmandu on Wednesday."A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Global warming and/or an earthquake in Tibet may have caused a large chunk of a glacier to break off and fall into the valley below, experts surmise," Tharoor said in a post on X.Tharoor added that the flooding had destroyed at least 19 motorable bridges and washed away around 40 km of the Betrawati–Rasuwagadhi highway. Eight operational hydropower projects were also reported to have sustained heavy damage.Tharoor said he supported the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance to Nepal, adding that the country would need substantial help in responding to the destruction.He also expressed concern over the loss of life and those still missing, including Indians affected by the disaster."I fully support the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance.Nepal needs all the help it can get. My heart goes out to the victims and their loved ones, who include large numbers of Indian tourists, including a hundred performing the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra. Prayers for the missing; may they be rescued soon," Tharoor said.The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in Nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in Tibet, according to authorities.The scale of destruction has hampered rescue operations, with Nepalese officials reporting that dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40 kilometres (25 miles) of roads damaged.The Nepalese Army launched helicopter operations on Thursday morning, rescuing more than 100 people from flood-affected areas, army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said. At least eight foreign nationals were also airlifted to Kathmandu, while army teams evacuated people trapped inside facilities associated with the Trishuli hydropower project.India is also coordinating efforts to assist its nationals stranded in the affected areas. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said five major groups, comprising around 288 Indian nationals, had been identified.“ The first group of 73 people who are working on the Trishuli-1 power project. Then, two separate groups of 37 and 49 nationals from Tamil Nadu, who traveled for Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Samrat and Fly Everest Travels. There is a group of 32 Indian nationals from West Bengal who traveled with the help of Samrat Travels in Timure, which is in Rasuwa district.”“Then, a group of 61 Indian nationals from different states and then a group of 33 Indian nationals from Kerala. These are five major groups who comprise, by and large, 288 people that we are talking about,” he added.Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah and offered India’s assistance for rescue and relief operations.“India is prepared to provide Nepal with all possible types of humanitarian assistance,” PM Modi said, adding that Indian teams were coordinating rescue and relief efforts.The United Nations is also supporting the response, with agencies deploying personnel to assist local authorities. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric warned of a “massive humanitarian need” as rescue and relief operations continued.The disaster has also renewed concerns over the Himalayan region’s exposure to extreme weather events and glacial hazards, particularly in areas where difficult terrain and damaged infrastructure can complicate emergency response.
Article Summary: A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in Nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in Tibet. India is also coordinating efforts to assist its nationals stranded in the affected areas.

Water rose 30 feet and at least 160 people were killed, while hundreds of others, including scores of Kailash Mansar-ovar pilgrims from India, remained missing after a flash flood and mudslide of unprecedented scale in Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers tore through a part of Nepal-Tibet border on Wednesday morning. It swept away settlements, hydropower units and the pilgrim route.Nepal Police put the toll at 157, while Chinese authorities reported three deaths and 265 people missing in Tibet’s Gyirong county. Nepal Police said 579 others — 466 foreigners from 28 countries and 113 Nepalis — remained untraced, including at least 133 Indians. Among the missing were at least 37 NRIs. Frighteningly, as many as 33 bodies were found 150km downstream at Chitwan, showing how far the dea-dly waters carried victims.Among the missing foreigners were 54 Americans, 34 Australians, 33 Britons, 24 Canadians, 19 Malaysians and 8 Koreans.Many were Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims, with nearly 400 of them, including the Indians, preparing to cross the Nepal-Tibet border or travelling through the region when the flood struck.Rescue personnel battled poor weather, mud, washed-out roads and high river levels even as authorities moved families from vulnerable settlements to safer locations.Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal told parliament that 29 police personnel and 44 soldiers remained untraced after floodwaters swept away their barracks in Rasuwa, while customs officials, hydropower workers and other employees stationed near the border were also missing. At the 20MW Langtang Khola Hydropower Project, dozens of workers are out of contact. The torrent also swept away or inundated security posts, customs facilities, banks and other establishments along the river corridor. Nepal PM Shah appealed for patience and unity as the Nepali Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force deployed helicopters, drones, boats and ground teams for search-and-rescue operations.Across the border, floods and mudslides severed several roads, communications and electricity around the (dry) Gyirong port, a key Nepal-Tibet crossing used by Kailash-Mansarovar pilgrims. Chinese president Xi Jinping called for “all-out efforts to search and rescue people who are missing”.The flood destroyed critical infrastructure across northern and central Nepal, with preliminary govt estimates showing at least 19 bridges and around 40 km of roads damaged or washed away; 13 hydropower projects were hit, and around 200 trucks were lost. The Nepal govt declared the worst-affected areas disaster-hit zones for the next 3 months and ordered authorities to provide free treatment to the injured.
Article Summary: Nepal Police put the toll at 157, while Chinese authorities reported three deaths and 265 people missing in Tibet’s Gyirong county. Nepal Police said 579 others — 466 foreigners from 28 countries and 113 Nepalis — remained untraced, including at least 133 Indians. Among the missing foreigners were 54 Americans, 34 Australians, 33 Britons, 24 Canadians, 19 Malaysians and 8 Koreans.

NEW DELHI: Responding to letters written by SC judge Sandeep Mehta complaining against Rajasthan high court acting chief justice (ACJ) Sanjeev Prakash Sharma and seeking his transfer outside the state, CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJ’s response.Justice Mehta wrote three letters in as many weeks pleading for the transfer of Justice Sharma, who is retiring Sept 26, and appointment of a regular chief justice. Justice Mehta also complained as to why CJI Kant had not acted on his fervent pleas.Justice Mehta, who also hails from Rajasthan HC, has accused Justice Sharma of lacking in leadership qualities and alleged there was maladministration and malpractice on both judicial and administrative sides of HC.CJI Kant told TOI that the matter can be resolved only as per the established mechanism. “The Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media,” he said. He also released a public statement Wednesday decrying the attempt to hold a public trial over allegations made by one judge against another.Contents of the letters cannot be adjudicated in public domain and that judge concerned must be given a fair opportunity to place his response before any conclusion is reached.The fact that allegations have been made, therefore, cannot by itself be treated as a finding against the judge,” CJI Surya Kant’s statement said.The established mechanism for inquiring into allegations of an Supreme Court or High Court judge is the constitution of an in-house committee — comprising judges — by the Chief Justice of India, if he finds the response of the judge accused of misdemeanour or corrupt practices unsatisfactory and feels the charges are serious enough to warrant a deeper probe.CJI Kant, who is on a three-day official visit to Germany, also told TOI that he has already sought a response from Justice Sharma following the letters from Justice Mehta, who has alleged that there is “clear evidence of favouritism” by Justice Sharma. Justice Mehta’s complaints are being examined, CJI Surya Kant said.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant Wednesday said he has sought the ACJ’s response. Article Title: Dissidents push for Hindu Pradesh Congress Committee chief to end Punjab crisis

NEW DELHI: Congress is again mulling the idea of appointing a Hindu state president in Punjab amid a push from dissidents for a compromise to end the turmoil in the state unit.Well-placed sources said the deadlock in the dissidence-ridden organisation has cast a cloud over the upcoming election campaign, and the party brass is cut up about the unsuccessful fire-fighting efforts of key managers.A group of dissidents that includes senior netas like Charanjit Channi and Sukhjinder Randhawa has been seeking the replacement of state chief Amarinder Raja Warring ever since the AICC announced a clutch of poll-related panels while sticking with Warring at the helm two months ago.Now, sources said, the dissidents themselves have proposed that a Hindu Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) chief be appointed. This group has also conveyed that they will be on board with such a replacement, even though each one of them has been fancying their chances till now, they added.With the state chief and the leader of opposition both belonging to the Jatt Sikh community, the idea of a Hindu PCC chief is meant to bring balance to the organisational set-up.This was the original idea before the AICC decided to retain Warring at the top.An insider said the party is looking at its options and may have to make some change in the leadership position — either the Punjab chief or AICC in-charge, or both. While it is too close to the elections for such an organisational overhaul, the sources said the crisis has to be defused.Sources also dismissed the notion that Rahul Gandhi will soon kickstart the state campaign in the form of a bus journey, arguing that the bus would bring all the squabbling netas together and, thereby, enforce peace.A party manager said Rahul will only start the bus journey after the organisational bickering is over.“The campaign will be about the state and state Congress. It needs an agenda so that the party can set a narrative for voters,” he said. “The state netas will have to come together and draw up a plan for winning the election together. Only then will Rahul get into it,” the party functionary said.Also, Rahul will be a part of the bus campaign for 2-3 days, and state netas will steer the rest of it for around 20 days. While Congress was hopeful of its chances in the AAP-governed state, persistent infighting in the local unit has raised concerns about its prospects.Inputs that forces like jailed MP Amritpal Singh’s “Waaris Punjab De” may be gaining ground have further alarmed some strategists.
Article Summary: Dissident netas, including Charanjit Channi, have been seeking the replacement of state chief Amarinder Raja Warring. The dissidents themselves have proposed that a Hindu Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) chief be appointed. The idea of a Hindu PCC chief is meant to bring balance to the organisational set-up.

JAMMU: Security forces launched a joint search operation in the remote, hilly hamlet of Sumb in J&K’s Samba district after receiving information that a wireless set had been briefly activated in the area and satellite communication was detected around 1pm Tuesday.“The reported activation of Iridium satellite sets raised suspicion among security agencies, following which a combined team of the Army, police, and personnel from other forces rushed to Sumb’s Makoli village and initiated extensive searches in and around the area,” an official said Wednesday.“Terrorists often switch off such communication devices after contacting their handlers across the border,” said a source, adding that Iridium sets can be used on smartphones through the “Iridium GO!” mobile application, which creates a local Wi-Fi network that an iOS or Android phone can connect to.The operation continued until late Tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found. Security was tightened along all routes leading to Sumb, with J&K Police and Village Defence Guards maintaining strict vigil, officials said.The hilly area of Sumb is considered strategically important from a security perspective as the route runs along the Basantar river and leads towards the India-Pakistan international border. Due to its proximity to the border, Samba district is a hotbed of terrorist activities. It serves as a gateway district for ultras heading towards Kashmir Valley via the upper reaches of Samba-Udhampur-Doda-Kishtwar.

At a time when many Hindu devotees traditionally give up non-vegetarian food during 'Sawan', fish has acquired an unlikely political importance in Uttar Pradesh.The row began earlier this month with Uttar Pradesh minister and Nishad Party chief Sanjay Nishad's remark that fish cooked without garlic and onion could be considered vegetarian. It escalated on August 23, when a video purportedly showing fish being prepared at a Nishad community event in Ayodhya, attended by UP Congress president Ajay Rai, surfaced on social media.But behind the sparring over what was - or was not - on Rai's plate lies a larger electoral calculation. The Nishad vote has shifted political loyalties before, and with the BJP seeking to retain its non-Yadav OBC coalition and the opposition trying to prise open that support, the community could once again become an important factor in the 2027 contest.The controversy began earlier this month when Sanjay Nishad said at a programme: "Bina lahsun-pyaz ki bani machhli shakahari hai."The remark came during Sawan, a month when many Hindu devotees observe dietary restrictions, and quickly attracted attention because of the community he represents. Nishads have historically depended on rivers and water bodies for fishing, fish-rearing, boating and related livelihoods, making food and fishing practices part of a broader social and economic identity.Then came Ayodhya.On August 23, UP Congress president Ajay Rai travelled to Tarun, around 30 km from Ayodhya, after visiting Hanumangarhi, reciting the Hanuman Chalisa and offering prayers at the Ram temple. He attended a programme organised by members of the Nishad community. A video showing fish being prepared at the venue subsequently surfaced.The timing and location gave the BJP an opening.BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary described the alleged fish feast as "highly condemnable and unforgivable", while Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath accused Rai of "duplicity" for visiting a temple and then attending a fish feast during Sawan."You saw the conduct of the Congress state president yesterday. He goes to Hanumangarhi for darshan and, after coming out, enjoys a fish feast and then shouts 'Ram-Ram'," Adityanath said.Rai denied eating fish and challenged the CM to produce evidence. "If he can produce any pictures, I will be ready to resign immediately," he said.Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera defended the hosts, saying they belonged to the Nishad community and had their own traditions of eating and drinking.Later, cabinet minister Om Prakash Rajbhar entered the controversy, backing Nishad's earlier claim and asking Congress to clarify whether the fish allegedly served at the event had been cooked with garlic and onion."Sanjay Nishad machhli ke mahir hain, unhe zyada jaankari hai, hum thode kam hain," Rajbhar said.The political argument, however, goes well beyond the menu at one event. The larger story is the political importance of the community that hosted it.The Nishads are a cluster of riverine communities whose traditional livelihoods have been closely tied to rivers, ponds and other water bodies. Community organisations have increasingly used the term 'jal kisan', or water farmers, to describe this relationship.Fishing, fish-rearing, boating and the sale of fish have historically been central to these communities' economic lives. Questions over access to water bodies, fishing rights, sand mining and regulation of traditional occupations therefore have a direct political resonance.The term Nishad is also used as an umbrella for several communities and sub-castes, including Mallah, Kewat, Bind, Kashyap, Dhimar, Batham, Kahar, Manjhi and Turaha. Not all of these communities necessarily identify themselves as Nishad in the same way.In Uttar Pradesh, Nishads are classified among the Other Backward Classes (OBCs).Political estimates put the core Nishad population at around 4.5-5 per cent of the state's electorate. Estimates that include a wider set of related riverine communities put their combined share considerably higher.There is no recent official caste census providing a definitive figure, but the community's electoral importance comes less from its statewide percentage than from its concentration.Nishad voters have a significant presence across the Ganga-Yamuna belt and eastern Uttar Pradesh, including Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Azamgarh, Ballia, Mau, Ghazipur, Mirzapur, Bhadohi, Jaunpur and Prayagraj, besides parts of Sultanpur and Fatehpur.The community is considered electorally influential in more than 160 Assembly constituencies, with around 80 seats often identified as having a particularly substantial Nishad presence.That geographical concentration explains why a community accounting for a relatively small share of the state's electorate can command such political attention.The Nishad political identity is also deeply connected to stories from the Hindu epics.In the Ramayana, Nishadraj Guha, the boatman-king, is described as an ally of Ram during his exile. Guha receives Ram, Sita and Lakshman and helps them cross the Ganga.For the Nishad community, the story has long been invoked as a marker of their place within the Ram narrative — not as an identity created by contemporary politics, but as an older cultural association that acquired renewed political meaning during the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.The community also invokes Ekalavya from the Mahabharata, who is traditionally identified as belonging to the Nishad community. His story - of a skilled archer seeking to learn from Dronacharya and ultimately giving his thumb as guru dakshina - has come to represent a different strand of Nishad memory: talent, exclusion and the struggle for recognition.The two figures capture contrasting elements of the community's epic imagination: Nishadraj represents proximity to and loyalty towards Ram, while Ekalavya represents ability denied recognition.These narratives have subsequently been woven into the community's assertion of a distinct historical and social identity.Sections of the community found their cultural resonance in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.As the campaign for a Ram temple in Ayodhya gathered momentum in the late 1980s and early 1990s, Nishad organisations and leaders participated in the wider mobilisation. The story of Nishadraj Guha gave the movement an immediate cultural connection for sections of the community, while the broader call for 'Ram Rajya' resonated with those who saw the temple campaign as a civilisational and cultural cause.The political landscape changed sharply after BJP leader LK Advani's Ram Rath Yatra in 1990, which transformed the temple issue into a mass political movement. The demolition of the Babri Masjid on December 6, 1992, further entrenched Ayodhya as a defining issue in BJP politics.As the BJP expanded its support among non-Yadav OBC communities, sections of the Nishad community also moved towards the party.But that support did not become a permanent political contract.Among sections of Nishad political opinion, a recurring grievance emerged: the community had supported the Ram movement but did not receive a commensurate political return.The complaint has, at various points, extended to BJP leaders associated with the Ram movement, including Advani and former UP CM Kalyan Singh, with Nishad voices arguing that their support for the Ram cause did not translate into adequate representation or resolution of longstanding demands regarding representation and farming on the riverside.In the coming years, the same community that participated in the Ram movement subsequently moved towards the Samajwadi Party, created its own political organisation and entered into an alliance with the BJP.That fluidity became particularly visible in the 1990s.Before the emergence of the Nishad Party, the strongest political association for sections of the community came through the social-justice politics of the Samajwadi Party.Phoolan Devi became the most recognisable symbol of that phase.A Mallah woman from Uttar Pradesh, Phoolan Devi contested the Mirzapur Lok Sabha seat on an SP ticket in 1996 and won. She retained the seat in 1999.Her rise gave the community an unusually prominent political figure and turned caste identity into a language of representation.Her political legacy continues to be invoked in Uttar Pradesh.The next major shift came in 2016, when Sanjay Nishad founded the Nirbal Indian Shoshit Hamara Aam Dal, popularly known as the Nishad Party.The party sought to consolidate riverine communities and give political expression to demands involving reservation, representation, fishing rights and livelihoods.Its first major electoral breakthrough came in an unlikely place.In the March 2018 Gorakhpur Lok Sabha bypoll, Praveen Nishad, Sanjay Nishad's son, contested as an SP-backed candidate and defeated the BJP.The result was politically significant because Gorakhpur had been Yogi Adityanath's parliamentary stronghold for five consecutive terms.The defeat demonstrated that the BJP's support among non-Yadav OBC communities could be disrupted when Nishad mobilisation combined with the SP's wider social coalition.But the equation soon changed again.Before the 2019 Lok Sabha election, the Nishad Party moved into the BJP-led NDA. Praveen Nishad joined the BJP and contested the Sant Kabir Nagar Lok Sabha seat on a BJP ticket, winning the election.The BJP-Nishad Party alliance became an important part of the BJP's strategy to consolidate non-Yadav OBC support in eastern Uttar Pradesh.The BJP and Nishad Party continued their alliance into the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly election.The BJP won 255 seats, while the Nishad Party won six. The NDA retained power with 273 seats in the 403-member assembly.For the BJP, the alliance helped reinforce its eastern Uttar Pradesh coalition.For Sanjay Nishad, however, being part of the government brought a different problem: once an ally enters government, its demands are increasingly judged against what it can actually secure from that government.The biggest unresolved issue remained the demand for Scheduled Caste status for sections of the Nishad community.Sanjay Nishad has repeatedly pressed the BJP government on the demand.On August 18, 2026, just months before the 2027 elections, he escalated the issue again, saying he was prepared to give up his ministerial position if necessary.His friction with the BJP had also become visible after the 2024 Lok Sabha election, when he blamed BJP leaders for his son Praveen Nishad's defeat in Sant Kabir Nagar.Praveen, who contested the seat on a BJP ticket, lost to the Samajwadi Party's Laxmikant Pappu Nishad.The result was another reminder that a BJP-Nishad Party alliance does not necessarily translate into a uniform Nishad vote.That fluidity is what the opposition is trying to exploit ahead of 2027.In March 2026, it appointed Sadhvi Niranjan Jyoti as chairperson of the Uttar Pradesh Backward Classes Commission. The move came alongside the BJP's continuing alliance with the Nishad Party.The SP responded by appointing Phoolan Devi's sister, 67-year-old Rukmini Devi, as president of the party's Uttar Pradesh women's wing. The appointment was seen as part of Akhilesh Yadav's PDA — Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak — outreach ahead of the 2027 election.Rukmini Devi subsequently attacked Sanjay Nishad, questioning what he had delivered for the community while being part of the government.The appointments show that the competition for the Nishad vote is not merely about alliances. It is a contest over who represents the community's political memory.Congress, on the other hand, has a more difficult task because its organisational presence among Nishads is weaker.Its August outreach in Tarun was therefore significant. Ajay Rai's visit to the Nishad community programme was an attempt to establish a direct connection with the community.The party's subsequent defence of the event, that the hosts were Nishads with their own food traditions, also allowed Congress to frame the controversy around community identity and traditional livelihoods rather than solely religious conduct.For the SP and Congress, the broader argument is that the Nishad vote is not synonymous with the Nishad Party.The Vikassheel Insaan Party (VIP), led by Bihar-based Nishad leader Mukesh Sahani, adds another layer to this contest.VIP entered Uttar Pradesh politics in the 2022 assembly election, seeking support among Nishads and other Extremely Backward Classes, particularly in Purvanchal.The party did not emerge as a major electoral force, but its campaign showed how smaller caste-based parties can complicate a close contest.VIP contested more than 100 seats, primarily in eastern Uttar Pradesh, and said its candidates polled more votes than Congress candidates in 15 constituencies, including Bairia, Bansdih, Phephna, Alapur, Jalalpur, Ghanghata, Balha, Shahganj and Kerakat.Its relationship with the BJP has been politically fluid rather than a straightforward alliance in Uttar Pradesh.Sahani has been a vocal critic of the BJP at various points. However, in neighbouring Bihar where the Nishads remain relevant across the seats in the Ganga area, his political trajectory has repeatedly shifted. VIP contested as part of the opposition Mahagathbandhan in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, switched to the NDA for the 2020 Bihar assembly election (winning 4 seats and entering the cabinet), but was dropped from the NDA in 2022 after contesting against the BJP in UP. In last year's Bihar polls, his party failed to secure any seat.However, in upcoming polls in UP, a few thousand votes in its favour can alter the results in close constituencies.The fish controversy may fade, but the political question it has exposed is unlikely to disappear.The BJP has the advantage of a long association with the Ram movement, an established organisational network and an alliance with the Nishad Party.The SP is seeking to revive the community's social-justice connection through Phoolan Devi's political legacy and the PDA framework.Congress is attempting to build a direct relationship with Nishad voters, while smaller parties such as VIP can potentially fragment the vote.For the Nishads themselves, however, the choice is unlikely to be framed around a single issue.Their political history has moved from the epic memory of Nishadraj and Ekalavya, to participation in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, to the social-justice politics associated with Phoolan Devi, to the rise of the Nishad Party, its alliance with the BJP and subsequent friction over representation and reservation.The lesson from that history is clear: the Nishad vote has never been permanently owned by one party.In 2027, the contest will be over whether Ram and the BJP's organisational alliance can outweigh demands for reservation, representation and livelihoods - and whether the opposition can convert those demands into votes.
Article Summary: The Nishad community finds itself at the centre of the fish row in Ayodhya ahead of 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly polls. The row began earlier this month with Uttar Pradesh minister and Nishad Party chief Sanjay Nishad's remark that fish cooked without garlic and onion could be considered vegetarian. It escalated on August 23, when a video purportedly showing fish being prepared at a NishadCommunity event, attended by UP Congress president Ajay Rai, surfaced on social media.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday launched the 'Lokmata Ahilyabai Matrushakti Yatra' scheme and flagged off special buses to provide free travel facilities to women aged 60 years and above in the state.Speaking at the launch event in Lucknow, CM Yogi said the scheme was aimed at making the journey of women more convenient and dignified and strengthening their self-reliance."The maternal power that has eased the path of family and society throughout her life--our resolve to make her journey smooth and dignified is being realised in the double-engine government," the Chief Minister said.Under the scheme, women aged 60 years and above will be provided free bus travel facilities. The Chief Minister also said that on Raksha Bandhan, mothers, sisters and daughters would be provided free bus travel along with one accompanying person."The honour of maternal power and their convenience is our priority," CM Yogi said.The Chief Minister said the scheme has been named after Lokmata Ahilyabai Holkar, whom he described as an exemplary figure of women's self-reliance and good governance."At a time when the country was in the grip of the chaos caused by Mughal invaders, Lokmata Ahilyabai not only achieved the goals of good governance and preserved India's spiritual and cultural heritage but also set an exemplary standard for women's self-reliance," he said.CM Yogi said Ahilyabai Holkar had undertaken the restoration of several temples across the country that had been demolished or damaged by foreign invaders."Whenever the topic of women's self-reliance arises, we all recall the name of Lokmata Ahilyabai with deep reverence and respect," he said.The Chief Minister also launched a sharp attack on the previous governments in the state, alleging that women faced insecurity and lack of dignity before 2017."There was a time before 2017 when a particular slogan echoed among daughters, sisters, and mothers: '" CM Yogi said, referring to the Samajwadi Party.He alleged that the period was marked by concerns over women's safety and a lack of dedicated mechanisms such as integrated helplines, women's beat systems and women's help desks."There was no respect for them, let alone self-reliance; there were no integrated helplines, no women's beat systems, and no women's help desks," he said.CM Yogi further alleged that middlemen controlled pensions and scholarships and that mafia groups exercised influence over sectors including forest, sand, cattle and examination systems."Forest, sand, cattle, and exam-cheating mafias defined the state's identity; a mafia syndicate wielded power parallel to the actual government," he said.The Chief Minister said his government had, for the first time since Independence, formulated a comprehensive action plan aimed at integrating women, who constitute half of society, into governance schemes."This plan encompasses everything from a daughter's birth to her education, employment, and entrepreneurship, while also guaranteeing her safety and dignity; indeed, every scheme, decision, and budget of our government is dedicated to fulfilling these very objectives," he said.The Chief Minister had earlier announced the launch of the scheme in a post on X, saying the initiative was aimed at ensuring convenience and dignity for women."The maternal power that has eased the path of family and society throughout her life--our resolve to make her journey smooth and dignified is being realised in the double-engine government. Today in Lucknow, the 'Lokmata Ahilyabai Matrushakti Yatra' will be inaugurated, under which mothers and sisters of the state aged 60 years and above will be provided with free bus travel facilities," the post read."Additionally, on Raksha Bandhan, mothers, sisters, and daughters will be provided with free bus travel facilities, including one accompanying traveller. The honour of maternal power and their convenience is our priority," he added.The scheme comes as the Uttar Pradesh government seeks to expand measures focused on women's welfare, mobility and self-reliance.
Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath launched the 'Lokmata Ahilyabai Matrushakti Yatra' on Wednesday. Women aged 60+ to get free bus travel under the scheme. CM Yogi said the scheme was aimed at making the journey of women more convenient and dignified.

Article Title: 'Hijab on their heads, not minds': Owaisi calls Allahabad HC ruling 'attack on Islam'
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi on Tuesday criticised the Allahabad High Court's dismissal of a minor student's petition seeking permission to wear a hijab with her prescribed school uniform in Prayagraj. Calling the ruling an "attack on Islam", Owaisi questioned the court's authority to determine what is essential to the religion.Addressing the Jalsa-e-Rahmatul-lil-Alameen gathering at the AIMIM headquarters in Darussalam, Hyderabad, Owaisi said the ruling was inconsistent with the constitutional protections of religious freedom and freedom of expression. He also pointed to the ongoing Sabarimala case before the Supreme Court, where a nine-judge bench is examining questions surrounding essential religious practices.The AIMIM chief said, "A judgment came from the Allahabad high court. A girl was wearing a hijab to school, and the Court ruled that one cannot wear a hijab. I disagree with this High Court judgment; I do not concur with it. The Sabarimala case is already before the Supreme Court, where nine judges are deciding what is essential. Today's verdict violates Articles 25 and 19 of the Indian Constitution. Who are you to decide what is essential to Islam? Girls are wearing hijab on their heads, not on their minds.It is an attack on Islam."The remarks came after a division bench of Justices JJ Munir and Indrajit Shukla dismissed the student's petition challenging the school's refusal to allow her to wear a scarf over her uniform.The court observed that the petitioner had not produced religious scriptures or other material establishing that wearing a scarf was an "essential" part of her religion, such that its absence would affect her faith. It also noted that photographs submitted before the court showed other students from the same religious community attending the school without scarves.The bench held that where a dress code is uniform, non-discriminatory, adopted in good faith and intended to maintain discipline and institutional identity, determining the uniform primarily falls within the school's jurisdiction.The court further said that the student's previous practice of wearing a scarf in lower classes without objection did not create a permanent or enforceable right to require the school to alter its uniform policy. It clarified that the school was not curtailing her freedom of faith but was enforcing institutional discipline, with the uniform forming an essential part of that discipline.The student had completed Class 10 at the same school and sought admission to Class 11. She told the court that she had worn a scarf over her school uniform since Class 6 and that the school had never objected to it.However, when she sought admission to Class 11, the school management informed her that wearing a scarf violated its dress code and refused admission on that ground.

Article Title: Was PoK's Skardu airbase next after Sargodha? Ex-CDS Chauhan reveals why India switched targets

NEW DELHI: Did India plan to strike Pakistan-occupied Kashmir’s Skardu airbase after targeting Sargodha? Former chief of defence staff General Anil Chauhan has revealed that Indian forces had cleared Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan as a possible target during Operation Sindoor but had to change plans because of “bad weather”.Chauhan, who was heading the military when Operation Sindoor was carried out, made the remarks while speaking at the Vivekananda International Foundation on Operation Sindoor and its aftermath.Recalling the counterterror operation, former CDS Chauhan said, "Once the Pakistanis had picked up the phone and said they wanted to talk at about 10 AM. The Air Chief asked me whether he should strike Sargodha, I said, Go ahead... I said, could you please identify two more targets, so one of the targets he identified was Skardu.""We gave a yes, but after some time, the weather was bad over it and they had to change over to Bholari," he added.Chauhan also clarified that Indian forces “did not target” Pakistan’s Kirana Hills, an area reportedly linked to a nuclear facility.He backed Air Marshal AK Bharti, who was the then Director General of Air Operations (DGAO) of the Air Force.Bharti had said on May 12 last year, “We have not hit Kirana hills, whatever is there.”Bharti was responding to questions about reports and social media claims that Indian forces had targeted Kirana Hills during Operation Sindoor.Chauhan said, “There was a small episode about what Air Marshal Bharti was asked, the Kirana Hills episode. I think I'll clarify this. On occasions, it's been asked whether Kirana Hills were hit; that is where their (Pakistan's) nuclear facilities are.”He said Bharti had “rightly clarified that we did not target Kirana Hills”.Chauhan explained that Indian forces had sent several loitering munitions towards Sargodha before the strikes. Kirana Hills is around 10 km north of Sargodha.“I can, maybe give a kind of an explanation... Before those strikes, we had sent in a lot of loitering munitions to Sargodha, and Kirana Hills is about 10 km north of Sargodha. So the loitering munition is looking for radars which are in and around Sargodha, and it has a time span, which means it will loiter for about two hours, and once it does not find a target, it comes down and hits somewhere,” the former CDS said.He added, “It must have come and hit one of those hills. So that could be one of the reasons as to what people asked... Because Pakistani media also showed some images in which there was smoke coming out from Kirana Hills.”India launched Operation Sindoor in May 2025, targeting nine major terror infrastructure sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) following Pakistan-sponsored Pahalgam terror attack on April 22.The counterterror strikes killed more than 100 terrorists. During the military confrontation, Indian forces also struck Pakistan's Sargodha airbase.Chauhan also underlined that Operation Sindoor is “still ongoing”.
Article Summary: Former chief of defence staff General Anil Chauhan reveals Indian forces had cleared Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan as a possible target during Operation Sindoor. Chauhan also clarified that Indian forces “did not target” Pakistan’s Kirana Hills, an area reportedly linked to a nuclear facility.

Article Title: No intention to quit politics, Nitin Gadkari clarifies

Statement taken out of context, not political: Gadkari’s office.

Statement taken out of context, not political: Gadkari’s office

NEW DELHI: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari ’s office said on Tuesday that his remark that the younger generation should be given more responsibility as “he could no longer take on as much work as before”, had been misinterpreted to suggest that he intended to quit politics.In a statement clearly prompted by speculation triggered by the minister’s comment on Sunday, his office emphasised that Gadkari’s remarks were “specifically about the Laxmanrao Mankar Trust”, an organisation established by him that runs Ekal Vidyalayas in tribal areas.Nitin Gadkari’s office said, “In that context, Gadkari said that he could no longer take on as much work as before and that the younger generation should be given an opportunity to take greater responsibility. Article Title: YouTuber Chhavi Varshney killed as SUV crashes into truck near Ujjain
Article Text:
Chhavi Varshney (Image Credit: Instagram)

Front of SUV mangled

Police begin probe

Bodies sent for postmortem





INDORE: A woman and her daughter were killed and three others seriously injured after an SUV crashed into a truck on the Ujjain-Garoth four-lane road near Ramakhedi village around 6 am on Tuesday.The deceased were identified as Sarika and her daughter Chhavi Varshney. Chhavi was a popular YouTuber and had more than two lakh followers on Instagram.Three other passengers — Surajpal, Sachin and Shyam — were seriously injured in the crash. All three were residents of Uttar Pradesh.According to preliminary information, the SUV was travelling behind the truck when its driver apparently lost control and rammed into the vehicle.The collision was so severe that the front portion of the SUV was completely mangled.One of the women was trapped inside the wreckage, prompting rescuers to make considerable efforts to pull her out. The injured were taken to the government community health centre in Barod and later referred to the district hospital in Agar.Barod police reached the accident site and began examining the circumstances that led to the crash.The collision caused chaos on the four-lane road for some time as rescue and relief operations were carried out.The bodies of Sarika and Chhavi were taken to the government hospital in Barod in an NHAI ambulance.Police said postmortem examinations would be conducted after the arrival of their family members. A case has been registered.
Article Summary: The deceased were identified as Sarika and her daughter Chhavi Varshney. Three other passengers — Surajpal, Sachin and Shyam — were seriously injured. The SUV was travelling behind the truck when its driver apparently lost control and rammed into the vehicle.

Article Title: 3 Telugu students en route to work killed in US crash; kin urge govt to help bring back remains
Article Text:
N Rahul, one of the three persons killed in the Florida accident

Dreams cut short

Poll Vote & Share your view What measures should be taken to ensure international student safety? Better safety awareness Stronger emergency support 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





HYDERABAD: Three students from the Telugu states, including one from Nizamabad, were killed in a road accident in Florida after their car rammed into a tree.The three were reportedly on their way to their workplaces, where they worked part-time jobs, when the accident occurred on Interstate 95 in Brevard County.The driver and the front-seat passenger died on the spot, while the third student, N Rahul of Navipet in Nizamabad district, who was seated in the rear, died while undergoing treatment at hospital. Rahul’s family was informed about the accident at around 3 am on Wednesday.The other two deceased were identified as Subramanyam Chaturvedula and G Anil. However, there was no further confirmation on where they hailed from.“All we want now is my son’s mortal remains to reach us at the earliest. They are not letting anyone go near him as the investigation is still ongoing. A Telugu association is helping us in the US, but we also hope the state govt steps in and ensures that my son’s body is brought back,” said Hari Babu, Rahul’s father.According to the family, Rahul had completed his master’s degree but stayed back in South Florida as he wanted to pursue a PhD.They said he was reluctant to return to India as he felt it would be difficult for him to return to the US due to a raft of changes being made to immigration laws.“He used to call us every other day. Even on the day of his accident, he was on the phone with his mother for a while and ended the call after his friends arrived to pick him up for work. That was his last call,” Rahul’s father added.Rahul had last come home three months ago to attend his sister’s wedding, it is learnt.Subramanyam and Anil are said to have been Rahul’s roommates. While one of them is said to be from Nalgonda, the other one is also from one of the Telugu states.According to sources, there was a fourth person in the car when the accident occurred, and he is currently in police custody. The details could not be independently verified.
Article Summary: Three students from the Telugu states, including one from Nizamabad, were killed in a road accident in Florida. The three were reportedly on their way to their workplaces, where they worked part-time jobs, when the accident occurred. The driver and the front-seat passenger died on the spot, while the third student, N Rahul, died while undergoing treatment at hospital.

Article Title: 18 rounds, 5 bullets: How Haryanvi singer Ankit Balyan who sang ‘Court Mein Goli Marenge’ was gunned down outside gym
Article Text:
Haryanvi singer Ankit Balyan was shot dead outside a gym in Shamli district.

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is most important for improving public safety? Stronger police presence Faster action against criminals Better surveillance and security systems 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





LUCKNOW: Haryanvi singer and YouTuber Ankit Balyan, 32, was shot dead in a point-blank attack outside a gym in Shamli district on Wednesday evening, with preliminary information indicating that around 18 rounds were fired at him.The incident took place around 7 pm near Aryapuri Nala Patri in the City Kotwali area. Police said the attackers arrived on two motorcycles and opened fire as Balyan stepped out of the gym and headed towards his Scorpio SUV.Also read: Delhi model dies after being stabbed multiple times in abdomen According to police and eyewitness accounts, four assailants were allegedly waiting outside the gym. Balyan reportedly tried to shield himself by moving towards the co-driver's side of the SUV as a wall obstructed the driver's side.The attackers allegedly pulled open the vehicle door and fired repeatedly at close range. Five bullets reportedly struck Balyan in the head and abdomen, while three hit the front windshield of his SUV.Balyan was rushed to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival. The attackers fled the scene, and police teams reached the spot soon after.Additional director general of police, Meerut Zone, Bhanu Bhaskar, reached Shamli along with senior officers to oversee the investigation.Superintendent of Police M P Singh said teams had been formed to identify and arrest the assailants.Police are examining CCTV footage from the gym and surrounding areas to identify the attackers and establish the sequence of events. Officials are also looking into a possible link to Haryana and investigating the motive behind the killing.The murder triggered protests by Balyan's family members, supporters and villagers. Protesters blocked the Delhi-Muzaffarnagar Road, around 50 metres from the shooting site, demanding immediate arrests and strict action against the accused.The situation became emotional after Balyan's body was brought to the road. His mother was seen holding her son's head in her lap and pleading with people not to disturb him, saying, "Don't speak, my son is sleeping."Balyan, a resident of Bantikheda village in Shamli, had more than 3.66 lakh YouTube subscribers and was known for his Haryanvi songs and performances. His videos often featured SUVs and firearms. He was also known for the song "Bhari Court Mein Goli Marenge Meri Jaan."He had attracted attention during a roadshow in Shamli in 2023, following which an FIR was registered against him and several supporters for alleged violations. There was also speculation that he was preparing to enter district panchayat politics, although police and his associates had not officially confirmed whether this was linked to the killing.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav condemned the murder, alleging that the law-and-order situation in Uttar Pradesh had been reduced to "zero". He also demanded that the possibility of political rivalry be investigated.Yadav described reports of Balyan's mother mourning with her son's body in her lap as "heart-wrenching" and said members of the Jat community were demanding the immediate arrest of the attackers.Police said no arrests had been made till late Wednesday night and that the investigation was underway.
Article Summary: Haryanvi singer and YouTuber Ankit Balyan, 32, was shot dead in a point-blank attack. The incident took place outside a gym in Shamli district on Wednesday evening. Police said the attackers arrived on two motorcycles and opened fire.

Article Title: Delhi model, 21, dies after being stabbed multiple times in abdomen inside home; heavy police deployed

The woman, identified as Muskan, a student and a model was alone at home when she was allegedly attacked. (Imran (L)

Heavy police deployment in area

NEW DELHI: A 21-year-old woman was found stabbed to death inside her home in west Delhi's Tilak Nagar on Wednesday evening, police said.The woman, identified as Muskan, a student and a model was alone at home when she was allegedly attacked. She suffered multiple stab wounds to her abdomen and other parts of her body.She was rushed to a hospital after police received a PCR call about the incident. Doctors declared her dead on arrival.Police have identified Imran, a gym trainer, as the main suspect. He fled after the incident, prompting multiple police teams to launch a search for him.The woman and the suspect had known each other for around one-and-a-half years, according to police.Relatives and neighbours told investigators that they had often seen the gym trainer in the area. They also said he had allegedly been pursuing Muskan, who was suspected to have rejected him."A woman, around 21 years of age, was stabbed to death when she was alone at her residence. CCTV footage is being examined and police investigation is under way," a senior police officer said.Investigators are examining CCTV footage from the area and scanning the woman's phone for possible leads.Police have also raided the gym where the suspect worked and his home. His family members and friends have been questioned as part of the investigation.The woman's parents appeared to be unaware of her friendship with the gym trainer, an officer said.Her body has been preserved in a mortuary and a postmortem examination is scheduled for Thursday morning.Tension was reported in the locality after the killing, with police deployment stepped up in the area.Police said the woman and the suspect belong to different faiths. Officials are maintaining a presence in the locality as the investigation continues.The motive behind the killing has not yet been officially established. Article Title: "Erika was photographed over his bloody mic": Candace Owens fires another shot at Erika Kirk as Tyler Bowyer’s Lindsay Clancy post sparks outrage
Article Text:
Candace Owens (Image via Getty)

Candace Owens challenges Tyler Bowyer over Erika Kirk comparison

Erika Kirk and Lindsay Clancy controversy intensifies

Candace Owens has sharply pushed back against a post by Turning Point USA chief operating officer Tyler Bowyer, who compared the public treatment of Erika Kirk with the support shown to Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy during her murder trial. Owens argued that criticism of fundraising efforts for Clancy can exist alongside criticism of TPUSA’s handling of Charlie Kirk’s death, adding another tense chapter to her long-running clash with the organization.The dispute began after Bowyer used X to contrast the backlash faced by Erika Kirk with the financial support surrounding Clancy’s legal case.His post stated, “strangle your three kids while evading your mental illness: ONE MILLION DOLLARS”.He then wrote, “lose your husband & father of your children but carry an organization with millions of followers on your back that recruits & registers young Patriots: A LIFETIME OF HARASSMENT”.Owens reposted Bowyer’s comments but rejected the comparison. She pointed to the commercial and fundraising activity surrounding Erika after Charlie Kirk’s death and questioned whether TPUSA should be weighing in on Clancy’s case at all.“You guys sold 50,000 t-shirts at the “event of the century” as Erika walked out to sparklers. You raised 40 million in one night at Mar-A-Lago as Erika was photographed over his bloody mic. It’s possible to disagree with fundraisers for Lindsay Clancy and also think TPUSA should sit this one out entirely.”Her response is significant because Owens has repeatedly criticized Erika Kirk and Turning Point USA since Charlie Kirk was killed. Rather than treating the controversy as a simple argument over Clancy, Owens has continued to use public posts to challenge how TPUSA has responded to the aftermath of Charlie’s death.The comparison comes as Clancy faces three murder charges in Massachusetts over the deaths of her children, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months. She has pleaded not guilty.The case has also raised difficult questions about mental illness and criminal responsibility. If convicted, Clancy could face life in prison without parole. A finding of not guilty because of a lack of criminal responsibility could instead result in commitment to a state mental health facility.Meanwhile, Owens has continued questioning Erika Kirk publicly on several fronts. She has criticized Erika’s interactions with journalist Brandy Zadrozny, challenged the privacy surrounding Charlie Kirk’s burial location and raised broader questions about the events following his death.Charlie Kirk, 31, was fatally shot on September 10, 2025, during a student question-and-answer event at Utah Valley University in Orem, according to the university’s account of the shooting. Tyler Robinson has been accused in the killing.The latest exchange shows that the conflict surrounding Charlie Kirk’s legacy is far from settled. Owens’ response has shifted attention back toward the conduct of TPUSA itself, while Bowyer’s original post sought to highlight what he described as a stark difference in public sympathy. With both sides continuing to speak publicly, the controversy is likely to remain a major point of discussion among Kirk supporters and Owens’ audience.
Article Summary: Candace Owens has sharply pushed back against a post by Turning Point USA chief operating officer Tyler Bowyer. Bowyer compared the public treatment of Erika Kirk with the support shown to Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy during her murder trial. Owens argued that criticism of fundraising efforts for Clancy can exist alongside criticism of TPUSA’s handling of Charlie Kirk's death.

Article Title: CCTV shows BJP MLA's daughter slapping cop at Karnataka temple
Article Text:
CCTV footage shows an altercation between an MLA's daughter and a police sub-inspector.





MANDYA: CCTV footage has emerged of an altercation between a police sub-inspector and the daughter of Tumakuru Rural BJP MLA B Suresh Gowda at a temple in Srirangapatna, days after the incident was reported.The footage shows Aishwarya, the MLA's daughter, in a heated exchange with PSI Savitha B Patil at Aarti Ukkada temple on August 12. During the argument, Aishwarya is seen using her phone and attempting to make a call before allegedly slapping the police officer.Savitha then appears to hit her back, following which other people at the spot intervene and separate the two.The incident occurred around 4.30pm during Bhima Amavasya celebrations and was reportedly triggered by a dispute over entry into the temple's sanctum sanctorum.Savitha, attached to the Mandya Women's Police Station, was deployed for crowd-control duty at the temple. According to her complaint, Aishwarya arrived with others and sought to enter the sanctum without waiting in the queue. When Savitha asked her to wait for a few minutes to avoid inconvenience to devotees, Aishwarya allegedly identified herself as the MLA's daughter and questioned why she was being stopped.The argument allegedly escalated, with Aishwarya abusing and slapping the PSI and threatening to affect her career. Savitha subsequently filed a complaint at Kyathanahalli police station.Police registered an FIR against Aishwarya under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for allegedly assaulting a public servant, causing simple hurt, intentional insult and criminal intimidation.Aishwarya has also filed a counter-complaint, alleging that the police officer abused her. Police said the allegations in the counter-complaint were being examined.Speaking to reporters, MLA Suresh Gowda apologised for his daughter's conduct if she was found to have made a mistake and said anyone at fault should face action under law. He said Aishwarya had gone to the temple with two young children and had requested permission to enter briefly as waiting in the queue could have caused difficulty for them.The MLA also said his daughter should have exercised restraint as a member of a political family and called for a departmental inquiry into the incident.Gowda further opposed VIP arrangements at temples, saying devotees should be treated equally and made to follow the same queue system to avoid inconvenience to the public and reduce pressure on police personnel.
Article Summary: CCTV footage shows Aishwarya, the MLA's daughter, in a heated exchange with PSI Savitha B Patil at a temple in Srirangapatna. The incident occurred around 4.30pm during Bhima Amavasya celebrations and was reportedly triggered by a dispute over entry into the temple's sanctum sanctorum.

Article Title: Dera chief Ram Rahim walks out of jail again, gets 21-day furlough in 17th temporary release
Article Text:
Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh has received another 21-day parole from jail.





ROHTAK: Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh walked out of Rohtak's high-security Sunaria jail early on Tuesday after being granted a 21-day furlough, marking his 17th temporary release from prison since his conviction in 2017.Ram Rahim, who is serving sentences in separate cases of rape and murder, left the jail at around 6.00am amid security arrangements. As per the information he has left for Sirsa based Dera headquarters. The latest furlough comes less than two months after he returned to Sunaria jail on June 26 on completion of a 30-day parole.The Ram Rahim was lodged in Sunaria jail in August 2017 after being convicted in the rape case involving two female devotees .He was subsequently convicted in other cases, including the murder of Sirsa-based journalist Ram Chander Chhatrapati.With Tuesday's release, Ram Rahim has now been granted parole or furlough on 17 occasions during his imprisonment. His repeated temporary releases have frequently triggered questions and criticism, particularly over the frequency of the relief granted to a convict serving sentences in serious criminal cases.Earlier this year, Ram Rahim was granted 40 days of parole in January. He was again released on a 30-day parole in May and returned to the Rohtak jail on June 26 after completing the period of his temporary release.The latest 21-day furlough once again brings the controversial Dera chief out of jail.His release is also being linked with Punjab politics which would witness assembly elections next year in February.
Article Summary: Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh has been granted a 21-day furlough from Rohtak's high-security Sunaria jail. The release marks his 17th temporary release from prison since his conviction in 2017. He is serving sentences in separate cases of rape and murder.

Article Title: Tipu Sultan cutout video with Pakistan reference sparks row in Karnataka, 23-year-old arrested
Article Text:
This video featured a Tipu Sultan cutout with a song referencing Pakistan





CHIKKAMAGALURU: Chikkamagaluru Police arrested a 23-year-old man on Tuesday for allegedly circulating a video featuring a Tipu Sultan cutout with a song containing references to “Pakistan” and “Mujahid”, prompting heightened security in the district, police said.Superintendent of Police Jitendra Kumar Dayama clarified that the action was not related to the installation of the Tipu Sultan cutout itself.He said a similar cutout had been installed at Tipunagara at the same location, around the same time and with the same dimensions in previous years.According to Dayama, police had earlier told organisers they could continue with arrangements followed over the past five to 10 years, but would not permit any new cutouts or decorations.The issue surfaced around 5pm to 5.30pm when the cutout was used as the backdrop in a video and a song containing a word referring to “Pakistan” and “Mujahid” was added, the SP said.The video was later circulated through multiple social media accounts and came to the police’s attention, ANI reported.Police registered an FIR under Sections 196 and 299 and traced the account that first circulated the video, following which the 23-year-old local resident of Tipunagara was arrested and is being produced before a magistrate, Dayama said.He allegedly shared the video as his WhatsApp status, sent direct messages to some Instagram accounts and other individuals, and uploaded a reel on his Instagram account, police said.Police are also probing the role of others who may have viewed, shared or recirculated the content."We are still in the process of ascertaining their role. If someone else also with intention did the same, then we will definitely arrest them and produce them," Dayama said.The SP said police were also trying to identify the person who originally created the video. A request has been sent to Meta for the relevant IP address as part of efforts to trace the original account.Dayama said the situation in Chikkamagaluru remained peaceful and police had spoken to community leaders. He said action would be taken against anyone attempting to create disturbances.Police social media monitoring teams at both the district and police station levels were also closely monitoring the situation, he said.More than 300 Home Guards, four Karnataka State Reserve Police (KSRP) platoons and local police personnel have been deployed for security, Dayama said. The forces will continue to monitor the situation during the function and the upcoming procession."Everything is peaceful, everything is calm, and this function will go on," Dayama said.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Chikkamagaluru Police arrest a 23-year-old man for allegedly circulating a video featuring a Tipu Sultan cutout. The video featured a song containing references to “Pakistan” and “Mujahid’ The action was not related to the installation of the cutout itself.

Article Title: Hair stylist killed as MUV rams scooter at Bengaluru signal

Victim identified as 33-year-old-hair stylist, Naveen





BENGALURU: A 33-year-old hairstylist died on the spot after a rashly driven car rammed into his two-wheeler on Kaggadasapura Main Road on Monday.CCTV footage of the accident showed the MUV driver ramming into victim Naveen’s gearless scooter, which was stopped at the Vijnananagar signal, throwing him into the air and killing him instantly.Police arrested the accused driver, identified as 63-year-old K Ramanan, a retired techie.Ramanan told police that he lost control of the vehicle out of anxiety and caused the accident.
