Article Title: Ghaziabad robbery: 2 held after gunfight, Rs 5 lakh of looted Rs 25 lakh recovered
Article Text:
Ghaziabad police apprehended two individuals following a gunfight on the Delhi-Meerut Expressway





GHAZIABAD: Ghaziabad police arrested two people for allegedly robbing Rs 25 lakh from a Meerut-based businessman on the Delhi-Meerut Expressway under the jurisdiction of Wave City police station.The arrests were made after a gunfight in which both accused received bullet wounds in their legs.According to police, the accused were identified as Saddam (20), a resident of Arthala, Sahibabad of Ghaziabad and Aasif (38), a resident of Meerut.A businessman carrying Rs 25 lakh in a bag was stopped right in the middle of Delhi-Meerut Expressway by armed men who blocked his Thar with two cars, held a pistol to his head and fled with the cashThe robbery took place around 7pm on Friday, when traffic continued to pass around the vehicle, oblivious to the crime the gang carried out inside the Thar.Gillaman, a Meerut businessman who owns a factory recycling waste material, was driving to Jafrabad in Delhi with his cousin Samad and relative Saleem to pay for supplies. He left Meerut around 5pm and reached Dasna in a couple of hours, when he was stopped on the expressway.Police registered an FIR against unknown persons under the section of 309 (4) (robbery) of BNS in Wave City police station.Priyashri Pal, ACP of Wave City said that on Tuesday early hours, the SWAT team and Crime Branch received information from an informer that the accused wanted in Case of a robbery of Rs 25 lakhs with Meerut based businessman on Delhi-Meerut Expressway, were roaming in the area on a Splendor motorcycle.On the information, the SWAT team, Crime Branch, SWAT team Nagar Zone, and Police Station Wave City police team started checking in the Wave City area.“During checking, 02 persons riding on one Splendor motorcycle without number plate were seen coming. When the police team tried to stop them, both motorcycle-borne persons, seeing the police checking and being surrounded by the police team, turned the motorcycle around and started fleeing back. When the police team chased them, they abandoned the motorcycle and started firing at the police team with the intention to kill. In retaliatory action, in the police encounter, both fleeing persons were injured after being shot in the leg and fell down. They were immediately sent to the hospital for treatment and their condition is stable,” she said.From the possession of the accused, the looted Rs 05 lakh was recovered along with 02 illegal country-made pistols of 0.315 bore, 04 live cartridges, 04 empty cartridges and a Splendor motorcycle without number plate were recovered.
Article Summary: A businessman carrying Rs 25 lakh in a bag was stopped right in the middle of Delhi-Meerut Expressway by armed men who blocked his Thar with two cars. The robbery took place around 7pm on Friday, when traffic continued to pass around the vehicle, oblivious to the crime.

Article Title: CM Suvendu Adhikari orders probe into Jadavpur University ‘anti-national’ graffiti
Article Text:
‘Anti-national’ graffiti on the Jadavpur University campus; CM Suvendu Adhikari





KOLKATA: CM Suvendu Adhikari on Monday ordered a probe into ‘anti-national’ graffiti on the Jadavpur University campus, telling the VC and the principal secretary of the higher education dept: “If the presence of such anti-national messaging and deranged psychotic drawings is verified, immediate steps must be taken to remove the graffiti, fix accountability and initiate strict administrative and legal action against those responsible. ”Posting the videos on his X handle, the CM said his office “has received concerning videos and photographic representations through the CM’s Grievance Cell from conscientious students of Jadavpur University, reporting instances of objectionable, sociopathic, violent and anti-national wall graffiti and drawings inside the Arts Division Boys Hostel premises,” adding, “Under no circumstances will campus premises be permitted to be used as platforms for spreading deranged propaganda and anti-India sentiment. ”The CM stated, “The Bengal govt strictly follows zero tolerance policy towards anti-national activities anywhere in the state, especially on campuses. The concerned dept and university administration must ensure stringent compliance and the preservation of academic integrity.”He added, “West Bengal’s educational institutions must remain centres of merit and discipline, not grounds for divisive rhetoric and unsocial activities.”
Article Summary: CM Suvendu Adhikari ordered a probe into ‘anti-national’ graffiti on the Jadavpur University campus. He told the VC and the principal secretary of the higher education dept: “If the presence of such anti-national messaging and deranged psychotic drawings is verified, immediate steps must be taken”

Article Title: Ladakh protests: Sonam Wangchuk leads Leh candle march, seeks inquiry report into 2025 violence
Article Text:
Activist Sonam Wangchuk led a candle march in Leh to remember last year's violent clashes





LEH: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Monday led a candle march in Leh as part of a month-long programme to remember those who died in the violent clashes in Ladakh last year, while demanding the release of the inquiry commission’s report into the September 2025 violence this month.Wangchuk said August 24 to September 24 would be observed to commemorate the events of September 24, 2025, when protests over statehood and inclusion of Ladakh in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution turned violent.A BJP office was set on fire during the unrest and at least four people were killed in police action that followed.Speaking on Monday, Wangchuk said the inquiry commission’s report should be released this month, arguing that the delay was affecting public confidence. He also said a “decisive meeting” between the Leh Apex Body (LAB), Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) and the Centre was expected in the first week of September to discuss Ladakh’s demands."This entire month, from August 24 to September 24, is being observed to honour and remember the events of 24 September 2025, which was a dark day. It was a day when five of our young men were martyred, and many others were injured, left disabled, or critically wounded.We began with a small candle march; it was kept small because His Holiness the Dalai Lama is currently in Ladakh. Once he departs, we will commemorate this month with much greater intensity," Wangchuk said.Recalling last year’s protests, he said Ladakh had been seeking its demands for six years and that a hunger strike began on September 10 after delays in addressing them."Regarding the situation over the past year: Ladakh has been demanding its rights for six years, but faced with delays and reluctance, people began a hunger strike on September 10 to make their voices heard peacefully. By the 15th day, when participants had to be hospitalised in critical condition, the public became deeply distressed and angry; circumstances arose, or were perhaps engineered, that led to some violence, and there is a pressing need for an investigation into this. "Wangchuk demanded that the report of the inquiry commission, headed by a retired judge, be made public, ANI reported."We are also calling for action regarding the Inquiry Commission led by a retired judge; a full year has passed, yet no decision has been reached. This delay is eroding public confidence. We hope that the Inquiry Commission's report will be released this month. Regarding the decisions concerning Ladakh's demands, discussed on May 22, no subsequent meeting has taken place to date. We hope that a decisive meeting will take place in the first week of September, as promised; otherwise, we will have to make our voices heard much more loudly, albeit peacefully," Wangchuk said.Wangchuk, who had spearheaded the protests along with the LAB and KDA, was detained for 170 days in Jodhpur Jail following the violence and was released in March 2026.The LAB and KDA have been demanding inclusion of Ladakh in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution. The Centre, meanwhile, has proposed that the Union Territory administration constitute an Autonomous Hill Development Council in each of Ladakh’s seven districts under a framework based on Article 371.Ladakh’s administrative map expanded from two districts to seven in April, when Sham, Nubra, Changthang, Zanskar and Drass were notified.The next round of talks with the Union Home Ministry is expected in September.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk led a candle march in Leh as part of a month-long programme to remember those who died in the violent clashes in Ladakh last year. Wangchuk said August 24 to September 24 would be observed to commemorate the events of September 24, 2025, when protests over statehood and inclusion of Ladakh in the Constitution turned violent.

In a statement suggesting that students’ protest and the Parliament session washout have the ruling BJP at a loss for strategy, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said “we” will not relent till PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah quit power under pressure. Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge said Modi and Shah will destroy the country and not leave anything for the coming generations. Kharge said Gujarat produced visionary leaders, but now “these two” are ruining everything.Rahul said the country is witnessing a fight between “those who give orders and those who want to express themselves”, adding that the country has started expressing itself after a lot of people behaved like “cowards” against the combine of RSS-BJP for a long time.“Our job is to make India express itself and break that order,” the Congress leader said, adding “we will drive them crazy”.Rahul and Kharge addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress, that seeks to create a common political strategy with non-Congress platforms of people’s struggle.Rahul said Modi is unable to sleep at night while Amit Shah, who was eulogised as Chanakya, did not come to Parliament for 20 days. “Because for the first time, they are feeling India’s expression. They realise this country will not stop expressing itself.It will break the RSS order.”“Till Modi and Shah give their resignations, they will not be able to sleep, we will keep them awake,” he said.He lashed out at the RSS as a “bunch of jokers”, and said the organisation has been reduced to being an instrument of big capital like Adani and Ambani, far from its original base of small businesses.The leader of opposition said Modi has messed up India’s national security and foreign policy, the latter because of the ignorant idea that he is making friends with the world leaders and foreign policy is about hugging them. He said Modi thought foreign leaders were his friends, and “they caught him”. He said India squandered a great opportunity presented by the Iran war to play the mediator, and the role was usurped by Pakistan.In what had the large audience from across the country in splits, Rahul illustrated Modi’s hugging by giving a bear hug to Rachnatmak Congress chief Sandeep Dikshit - who in turn asked Rahul jokingly “if he had thought he was hugging Italian PM Meloni”, and by enacting other practical jokes. He also cited a childhood anecdote of how then PM Indira Gandhi did not take seriously the US administration’s attempt to flatter her via the then First Lady.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi said ‘we’ will not relent till PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah quit power under pressure. Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge said Modi and Shah will destroy the country and not leave anything for the coming generations. Rahul and Kharge addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress.

Article Title: F-16 fighter jet crashes in Turkey during training flight, pilot safe
Article Text: A Turkish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a training flight in the northwestern province of Yalova on Wednesday, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported.According to the defence ministry, the pilot survived the crash after safely ejecting from the aircraft.In a statement posted on social media, the ministry said the aircraft went down during a routine training mission and that the pilot safely bailed out before the crash.The exact cause of the accident will be determined following a detailed investigation, the ministry added.A large number of ambulances and medical rescue teams were dispatched to the crash site following the incident, local media reported.Live footage broadcast by Turkish news channel NTV showed a fireball and thick black smoke rising from the wreckage, visible from several locations across the province.
Article Summary: A Turkish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a training flight in the northwestern province of Yalova. According to the defence ministry, the pilot survived the crash after safely ejecting from the aircraft. A large number of ambulances and medical rescue teams were dispatched to the crash site.

Article Title: Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp, Walt Nauta: 3 aides were allowed with Trump when he was moved into a catering truck during Turkey emergency
Article Text:
Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp and Walt Nauta are the closest aides allowed inside the catering truck that hid President Donald Trump in Turkey.

Who is Dan Scavino?

Who is Natalie Harp?

Who is Walt Nauta?

No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Apart from some low-ranking aides, only three individuals were allowed inside the truck, as they are believed to be the closest to the president: Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations. Washington Post reported that neither Marco Rubio nor Pete Hegseth nor Stephen Miller were allowed inside the truck that took TrumpThe catering truck moved under concealment from the Air Force One aircraft to a smaller Air Force C-32A before flying to Britain separately.Dan Scavino has been serving as the White House deputy chief of staff in the second Trump administration but his history with Trump dates back to 1992, when he worked as a caddie at a New York country club that Trump later purchased and turned into Trump National Golf Club Westchester. After graduating from college, Scavino worked his way up to become the golf club's general manager.He joined Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and went on to serve throughout the entire first Trump administration as White House Director of Social Media and later Deputy Chief of Staff for Communications.During that time, he was particularly known for managing Trump's personal social media presence and online strategy. He remained a central advisor at Mar-a-Lago following the 2020 election, worked as a senior official on the 2024 campaign, and returned to senior White House leadership upon Trump taking office again in 2025.Natalie Harp is an American political aide and former television presenter who serves as Executive Assistant to the President in Donald Trump's second White House administration. She is the one who handles the president's daily schedule and is always spotted with him. Known colloquially among campaign staffers and media outlets as Trump's "human printer," Harp earned a reputation for constantly accompanying him with a portable printer to feed him printed news articles, polls, and favorable commentary. In her role as executive assistant, she remains a member of his inner circle, assisting with his daily schedule and managing dictation for his social media accounts.Walt Nauta is a close political aide to Donald Trump and currently serves in his second White House administration as Deputy Assistant to the President and Director of Oval Office Operations. Nauta spent 20 years in the U.S. Navy, reaching the rank of Senior Chief Petty Officer. During his military career, he was assigned to the Presidential Food Service and eventually became a White House valet during Trump's first presidency. In that role, he acted as a personal assistant and "body man," handling day-to-day tasks like fetching beverages and managing travel details.After Trump left office in 2021, Nauta retired from the Navy and joined Trump's personal staff at Mar-a-Lago, continuing to work as his primary executive assistant and political aide. He later drew widespread national attention when he was indicted alongside Trump in June 2023 in the federal classified documents case, where prosecutors accused him of helping move and conceal boxes of sensitive materials.
Article Summary: No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations, are believed to be the closest aides to the president.

Article Title: Thailand visit, Suu Kyi access: Can Myanmar’s Min Aung Hlaing win political legitimacy?
Article Text:
Min Aung Hlaing in Thailand; Aung San Suu Kyi with ICRC official

Min Aung Hlaing's ascent to power

Significance of Aung San Suu Kyi

Why Thailand visit matters for Min Aung Hlaing - and how Bangkok differs from ASEAN

Can regional engagement help Min Aung Hlaing’s legitimacy push?

Min Aung Hlaing’s continuing legitimacy challenge

Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week, in a trip that carried significance beyond routine diplomacy. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency.That visit to Thailand coincided with another significant development in Myanmar. Aung San Suu Kyi , the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor. On August 3, Suu Kyi met Arnaud de Baecque, the International Committee of the Red Cross' (ICRC) resident representative in her country.Naypyidaw also released photographs of the meeting—the first official images of the former State Counsellor in years.Was the close timing of the two developments just a coincidence? For Min Aung Hlaing, who came to power by overthrowing an elected government rather than through the ballot box, both developments could be part of a broader effort to build political legitimacy and gain wider international acceptance.During his visit to Thailand, the 70-year-old former military leader sought to reassure his host, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, that Myanmar was “returning to democracy.”"Myanmar has now re-established itself on the path to democracy and is moving toward a better future," Min Aung Hlaing told Charnvirakul.The remarks stood in sharp contrast to the circumstances of his rise to the presidency. His claim that Myanmar is on a “democratic path” also comes against the backdrop of a bloody civil war triggered by the coup that brought him to power.According to the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, an independent organisation that documents arrests and casualties linked to the Myanmar civil war, more than 8,200 civilians had been killed and 31,645 people arrested by the regime's security forces as of August 5.Besides, the parliamentary elections under Min Aung Hlaing in late 2025 and early 2026 were also widely criticised as “neither free nor fair” as the army-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party swept the elections, winning 232 of the 263 contested seats in the lower house and 109 of 157 seats in the upper house. Ahead of the presidential election in April—Myanmar's first since 2018—he resigned from the military and was subsequently elected president.However, his transition to the presidency did little to ease international scepticism. Major democracies withheld congratulations following his victory.For Myanmar, Aung San Suu Kyi’s significance extends beyond her role as the head of the country’s first democratically elected civilian government in 50 years and the military’s toppling of her administration.For many inside and outside Myanmar, the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize laureate remains the country's most recognisable symbol of democratic rule and civilian legitimacy.In 2022, Suu Kyi was sentenced to 33 years in prison on a series of charges that her supporters and rights groups described as “politically motivated” and intended to prevent her return to politics. Later, her sentence was reduced to 27 years and, in April, to 18 years, while she was transferred to house arrest.Against this backdrop, the meeting with the ICRC representative was significant because it marked the first confirmed contact between Suu Kyi, 81, and an independent international organisation since her house arrest. It was also her first confirmed communication with the outside world since she wrote a letter to her son from prison in early 2024.Sreeparna Banerjee, an Associate Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation (ORF), agreed that both developments could be seen as part of Myanmar’s broader effort to “manage its international image,” but said it cannot be assumed that the moves were directly linked.“The timing is noteworthy, but it would be difficult to establish a direct connection between the two developments at this stage… Access to Aung San Suu Kyi after a prolonged period of isolation could signal some limited openness, while Min Aung Hlaing’s high-profile visit to Thailand demonstrates Myanmar’s attempt to expand diplomatic engagement,” Banerjee, whose work focuses on Myanmar and Thailand, told The Times of India.For Min Aung Hlaing, the bigger challenge remains turning such diplomatic engagement into wider political legitimacy and international acceptance.According to Banerjee, the visit was important for Min Aung Hlaing because it offered him a degree of political normalisation.“Being received at the highest level by an ASEAN neighbour allows him to project the image of a leader whose government is once again engaging with the region rather than remaining diplomatically isolated,” she said.Significantly, while Thailand and Myanmar are both ASEAN member states, Bangkok’s approach towards Naypyidaw differs from that of the rest of the 11-nation bloc of Southeast Asian states.Thailand has continued to engage with Myanmar despite ASEAN barring Min Aung Hlaing from its top-level meetings over the non-implementation of the Five-Point Consensus agreed with the grouping after he seized power.On this, Banerjee observed that the real value of Bangkok’s “bridge” diplomacy — acting as a bridge between Myanmar and ASEAN — would depend on whether Thailand can use it to encourage some meaningful progress on the Five-Point Consensus.Additionally, ASEAN is yet to recognise the results of Myanmar’s 2025–26 parliamentary elections. The bloc has also repeatedly called for Suu Kyi’s unconditional release, renewing the demand after her meeting with the ICRC official. The regime rebuffed this call too.For its part, Thailand has described its approach vis-à-vis Myanmar as one of “calibrated re-engagement” aimed at keeping dialogue open while responding to “realities on the ground.” Bangkok has also argued that Myanmar is essential to ASEAN unity and regional stability, provided it remains peaceful and stable.In addition to being barred from top-level ASEAN summits, Min Aung Hlaing faces Western sanctions over his role in toppling Suu Kyi’s government, the subsequent civil war, and the alleged persecution of the Rohingya minority in the Rakhine province.The Thailand visit was his fourth overseas trip since becoming president, following visits to India, China, and Laos. India was the only democratic country among the four destinations, underscoring the limited engagement he has so far had with democratic governments.Despite this, and close ties with Russia, he has remained largely isolated internationally.So, can his engagement with Thailand and his wider regional outreach — help him in his bid for greater international recognition and acceptance?Sreeparna Banerjee, the ORF Associate Fellow, suggested that even regional acceptance remains uncertain at this stage, despite such engagement being an important part of Myanmar’s quest for political legitimacy.“Naypyidaw appears determined to engage on its own terms rather than fully follow the ASEAN framework. Thailand's outreach may create space for dialogue, but whether this translates into wider regional acceptance remains uncertain,” she explained.She also highlighted that uncertainty over Myanmar’s regional acceptance stems in part from the fact that Singapore will take over the ASEAN chairmanship in 2027. The city-state has repeatedly called for full implementation of the Five-Point Consensus.This underscores the scale of the challenge facing Min Aung Hlaing in his bid for wider acceptance.For a leader who rises to power as Min Aung Hlaing did, securing international recognition is likely to remain a gradual and difficult process.The regime’s refusal to release Suu Kyi, a global icon, further complicates that effort.Engagement with neighbouring countries can provide an important opening, but broader recognition often depends on how other governments assess the resulting political situation. Yet for Min Aung Hlaing, this remains the only option to secure recognition.For now, engagement with Thailand may offer Min Aung Hlaing some diplomatic space, but whether it can translate into legitimacy for him remains uncertain.
Article Summary: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency. Aung San Suu Kyi, the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor.

Article Title: US Justice Department and FBI seize domains claimed to be used by China-linked hacking group targeting NASA, Federal Reserve and more
Article Text:
FBI says two platforms linked to China were used to hide the origin of attacks

FBI says platforms were used to hide the origin of attacks

Seized domains made QScan and QTRouter inoperable, DOJ says

The US Justice Department and the FBI have announced the seizure of internet domains linked to two hacking platforms allegedly used by a China state-sponsored cyber group to target critical infrastructure and sensitive networks. The platforms, known as QScan and QTRouter, were allegedly used to hide the origin of cyberattacks by routing malicious activity through compromised devices around the world. US authorities said the group's alleged victims included NASA, the Federal Reserve, the Department of Energy, the Department of Justice and the US Senate.According to court documents, US authorities have linked the platforms to a group known as QTFY, which they say is employed by China-based Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology Company. The Justice Department alleged that the group offered hacking services to paying customers, including China's Ministry of State Security and the People's Liberation Army.QScan allegedly scanned and automatically infected thousands of internet-connected devices, adding them to a network controlled through QTRouter.The compromised devices were then used to make malicious internet traffic appear to come from locations outside China, helping hackers conceal the origin of their activities, according to the Justice Department.“Today we announced the disruption of a global botnet and hacking platform used by Chinese state-sponsored hackers to target U.S. critical infrastructure,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “These tools were used by PRC cyber actors to hide the origin of their attacks.”The Justice Department said the seized domains were hard-coded into the QScan and QTRouter malware and were needed for important functions, including communication and authentication. As a result, the court-authorized domain seizures made both platforms inoperable, according to the department.“State-sponsored malicious hackers preying on America’s critical infrastructure will be stopped and prosecuted,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said. “We are here to ensure security for the American people and will use every tool we have to keep that promise.”The latest action follows several other operations by US authorities against alleged China-sponsored hacking activity. In 2025, the FBI said it removed PlugX surveillance malware from more than 4,000 computers in the US that had been infected by the group known as Mustang Panda. In 2024, authorities said they disabled a large network of compromised internet-of-things devices linked to Flax Typhoon. The FBI also disrupted another botnet in 2023 that it said was used by Volt Typhoon to conceal cyber activity targeting critical infrastructure.
Article Summary: FBI says platforms were used to hide the origin of cyberattacks. Seized domains made QScan and QTRouter inoperable, DOJ says. US authorities said the group's alleged victims included NASA, the Federal Reserve, the Department of Energy and the US Senate.

Article Title: Delhi model murder: Cops suspect Imran killed Muskan over her talking to another man
Article Text:
A friend of Muskan (left) had earlier claimed that Imran had been pursuing her for a long time.

What police suspect happened before the killing

Harassment angle under probe

The crucial timeline

Police hunt for Imran





NEW DELHI: A simmering two-month-long anger over another man may have culminated in a deadly confrontation inside a 21-year-old Delhi University student Muskan’s home, with police suspecting that jealousy drove Imran, a former gym trainer, to allegedly stab her multiple times, news agency PTI reported quoting officials on Thursday.The fresh details offer a possible motive behind the brutal killing of Muskan, a second-year student of Delhi University’s School of Open Learning and a model, whose murder inside her Tilak Nagar home had earlier triggered a search for her suspected attacker, Imran, 26.As per the PTI report, Muskan and Imran, who is currently unemployed, had known each other for around one-and-a-half years. Police suspect Imran had been angry with her for nearly two months because she was talking to another person.Police suspect that the tension eventually turned violent on Wednesday evening when Imran allegedly went to Muskan’s home while she was alone.An argument reportedly broke out between the two before Imran allegedly attacked her with a knife and fled, according to police.The investigation is also examining the nature of their relationship and what happened in the period leading up to the murder.As per the PTI report, police claimed that the two had met at a hotel on August 20, just days before the fatal attack.Aman, a friend of Muskan, had earlier claimed that Imran had been pursuing her for a long time and that her family had been informed about alleged harassment.The family, however, has not made a specific allegation against any other individual, and police are yet to establish the complete motive or sequence of events leading to the murder.The victim’s brother told police that Muskan knew Aqib alias Imran, who lived nearby, and suspected him of committing the crime, DCP (West) Hareshwar V Swami said, according to PTI.CCTV footage showed the accused entering the building at around 5.40pm, a police source said.The incident came to light after the house help found Muskan injured on the second floor and informed her family. A PCR call about the stabbing was received at Tilak Nagar Police Station at 7.24pm, the DCP said, according to PTI.Muskan was rushed to hospital, where doctors declared her dead on arrival.The post-mortem examination is expected to establish the exact cause and nature of her injuries.Imran remains absconding, and police have formed around 15 teams to trace him, according to PTI. Investigators are scanning CCTV footage and conducting raids at multiple locations.Police are also examining the circumstances surrounding the alleged confrontation and gathering evidence to establish exactly what happened inside the house.The case therefore goes beyond the question of who allegedly carried out the stabbing: investigators are now trying to establish what triggered the confrontation, whether jealousy over another person was the immediate provocation, and whether earlier alleged harassment formed part of a longer pattern.Police have not yet conclusively established the motive, and further investigation is underway.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Police suspect jealousy drove Imran, a former gym trainer, to allegedly stab Muskan multiple times. Muskan and Imran, who is currently unemployed, had known each other for around one-and-a-half years. Police suspect Imran had been angry with her for nearly two months because she was talking to another person.

Article Title: From Jantar Mantar to classrooms: How Gen Z and Gen Alpha are redefining student protest across India
Article Text:
Students of Jay Prakash Narayan Sarvodaya Balika Vidyalaya stage a road blockade protest over the shortage of teaching staff and the dilapidated condition of the road, in Lucknow on Monday. (ANI Photo)

From examination anger to everyday infrastructure

Members of different student organisations protest at Jantar Mantar.

The Gen Alpha question

The data behind the placards

When students become investigators of their own institutions

Social media has changed the protest itself

Humour, memes and the politics of a new generation

But student protest is not new

From campus politics to political recruitment

The government's response is changing too

The accountability effect

From Gen Z to Gen Alpha: What comes next?





NEW DELHI: Student protests are no longer confined to university campuses, examination centres or the familiar protest sites of the national capital. In 2026, the anger travelled from Jantar Mantar to government schools, tribal hostels, residential campuses, recruitment centres and even roads outside district collectorates.And something else has also changed: The age of the protesters.While Gen Z students and job aspirants drove the high-voltage protests over examination irregularities and recruitment processes, schoolchildren — many of them from what is broadly described as Gen Alpha — have increasingly begun demanding something much more immediate: A teacher in their classroom, a functioning toilet, electricity, drinking water, a safe road to school, a playground and, in some cases, simply a school building that is not falling apart.The protests are scattered, their demands are often intensely local and their methods vary. But together, they point to a larger shift: Students are increasingly seeing themselves not merely as beneficiaries of government education policies, but as stakeholders with the right to question how those policies are implemented.The change is visible in the outcomes too.A protest by schoolchildren in Hamirpur over the absence of a road to their school reached the Allahabad high court, which took suo motu cognisance of the matter and directed the forest department to expedite clearance for a crucial stretch of road.In Uttar Pradesh, protests over teacher shortages were followed by a move to draft a new policy for Sarvodaya schools.In Chhattisgarh, student protests over vacant teaching posts were followed by additional teachers being sanctioned and a principal being replaced.In Rajasthan, students studying in a cattle enclosure became the catalyst for a government decision to begin construction of a new school building.The question, therefore, is not simply why students are protesting.It is why authorities are increasingly being forced to respond.The most visible student mobilisation of 2026 began with a crisis of trust around competitive examinations.The Cockroach Janta Party-led agitation at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar transformed anger over examination irregularities into a much wider youth movement.Tens of thousands of young people participated in demonstrations, with the agitation eventually contributing to the resignation of former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on July 25. The protests also generated allegations of police excesses, leading the Supreme Court to constitute a panel to examine violence linked to the demonstrations.But the significance of the movement went beyond the resignation.It changed the vocabulary of student protest.The demand was no longer merely for a re-test or a correction in an examination process. Young protesters began speaking about institutional accountability, transparency, unemployment, public education and the credibility of the state.The movement also demonstrated the political power of an organised youth constituency.That distinction is important because the newer school protests have been even more direct.A 14-year-old does not generally march because of a policy paper. A child walks to the collectorate because there is no teacher for mathematics, no road to school or no usable toilet.That makes these protests harder to dismiss as ideological.The recent protests in Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand and other states show a striking pattern.The issues are basic.In Roorkee, students and teachers went to the municipal office and actually held a class inside the civic body’s premises to protest persistent waterlogging outside their school.Their message was simple: If the administration cannot make it possible for them to reach their classroom, they would bring the classroom to the administration.In Chhattisgarh, students at a government school in Pendrawan repeatedly protested because of a shortage of teachers. Nearly 400 students eventually blocked the Khairagarh-Dhamdha road. At one point, they remained on the road for hours and spoke directly to the education minister.“We do not want to leave our classes and sit on the road, but when there are not enough teachers to teach us, our studies and future are affected,” students said.The protest eventually produced movement on staffing, with the education department sanctioning additional teachers and replacing the principal.In another Chhattisgarh school, students locked the gate and protested over the absence of toilets and a boundary wall. In a Raipur school, students complained that the absence of a mathematics teacher had effectively prevented some of them from choosing mathematics as a subject.The protests aren't happening in a data vacuum.The Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+) NE-26 report — covering 24.7 crore enrolments and nearly 1 crore teachers nationally, at a pupil-teacher ratio of 24 — lays out exactly the kind of gaps students have been marching over.Only 67.4% of schools have internet and 63.1% have functional computers; digital libraries exist in just 7.1%. For children with special needs, only 40.1% of schools have appropriate toilets.The regional disparities are stark: Jharkhand runs 36 pupils per teacher; West Bengal has internet in only 19.7% of schools; Meghalaya has special-needs toilets in just 6.3% of institutions; Karnataka has 8,042 single-teacher schools. Nationally, UDISE+ records more than 29 lakh students enrolled in over a lakh single-teacher schools — even as 20,667 teachers sit in 5,663 schools with zero enrolment, a mismatch that captures the system's dysfunction in one statistic.State governments run 68.4% of India's 14.6 lakh schools; private unaided institutions account for 23.3%.The emerging protests also show students questioning authority inside schools.In Rajasthan’s Ajmer, girl students protested against their principal following allegations of molestation. In Jaipur, hearing- and speech-impaired students protested over unhygienic toilets, inadequate drinking water and a dilapidated school building. The Education Department subsequently removed the principal.In Madhya Pradesh’s Chhindwara district, 50-60 students travelled nearly 100 km with guardians and villagers to complain to senior officials about two guest teachers whose alleged conduct, according to the students, was affecting classes. Both teachers were removed and marked ineligible for future teaching appointments, while action was initiated against the principal.In Barwani, about 120 schoolgirls walked 18 km after alleging that their complaints about facilities, treatment and caste-related remarks had not been properly addressed. Officials eventually formed a committee to examine their grievances.These cases reveal another important change: students are learning how to escalate complaints.When an application fails, they march.When a march fails, they blockade.When local officials do not respond, they approach the collector.When the administration remains unresponsive, the issue reaches journalists, social media, courts or political representatives.That is not necessarily evidence that the protest culture is becoming more aggressive. It may also indicate that young people are learning the architecture of accountability.This generation is protesting in a completely different media environment from students of the 1970s, 1980s or even the early 2010s.A protest once needed a student union, pamphlets, posters, newspapers and political networks to become visible.Now a student needs a smartphone.The 2026 Gen Z protests demonstrated this transformation dramatically.Videos of police action, student speeches, memes and protest art circulated rapidly on Instagram, X and other platforms.International media documented how protesters themselves filmed clashes and turned the footage into short-form videos.Another described memes as a way of making protest accessible to people who might not otherwise follow politics.The significance lies in the change from broadcast protest to networked protest.Earlier, protesters depended on newspapers or television channels to tell their story.Today, they can document the event themselves.A student can upload a video of a broken toilet in the morning, tag a district official and have the issue circulating across local WhatsApp groups by afternoon.A photograph of children studying inside a cattle enclosure can become a political embarrassment.A video of a waterlogged school gate can force civic officials to explain why a problem has remained unresolved for years.Social media has therefore reduced the distance between grievance and visibility.It has also reduced the ability of institutions to control the narrative.The media ecosystem itself is changing. The Columbia Journalism Review recently described the protest wave as a challenge to India's traditional media environment, noting the growing influence of YouTubers and independent digital voices.The most unusual feature of the CJP movement was its use of humour.The very name “Cockroach Janta Party” turned an insult into a political identity. Memes, masks, reels and satire made the movement recognisable to young people who might otherwise have considered conventional political demonstrations tedious.The language of the street is increasingly the language of the internet.A slogan can become a meme. A meme can become a reel. A reel can become a mobilisation tool.And humour can perform a serious political function: It lowers the entry barrier.A young person who does not attend a traditional political meeting may share a meme about an examination leak, comment on a protest video and eventually turn up at a demonstration.India has a long history of students becoming catalysts for political change.In 1974, student protests in Gujarat over food prices, hostel fees and corruption grew into the Nav Nirman movement and eventually contributed to the resignation of chief minister Chimanbhai Patel.The Bihar student movement that followed brought Jayaprakash Narayan into active leadership and expanded into a national campaign against corruption, unemployment and political misrule.The JP movement became one of the defining political episodes preceding the Emergency.The anti-Mandal protests of 1990 showed another dimension: Students could become the frontline of intensely contested national policy debates.Later movements, including protests around citizenship, university autonomy and campus rights, again demonstrated the ability of students to push issues into the national political conversation.What is different today is not the existence of student anger.It is the speed at which that anger can travel.A 1974 student movement needed months of physical mobilisation to spread.A 2026 student movement can move from a school gate to a national conversation in hours.The political establishment has noticed.Political organisations and student wings have intensified membership drives on campuses following the Gen Z protests. In Mumbai, student organisations affiliated with different political parties have been competing for visibility and recruits.A Mumbai University professor described the shift in student politics this way: Young people were earlier treated largely as vote banks, but their political engagement is changing.“They are thinking more in a postmodern way, and no matter what political parties do, if their aspirations are not fulfilled, they will not remain permanent supporters.”That may prove to be one of the most consequential outcomes of the current wave.Political parties can recruit students.They cannot necessarily control them.The same young person can support one party on one issue and oppose it on another.That makes today's student electorate potentially more volatile and issue-driven.Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently asked Union ministers to spend time at universities and visit government schools in their constituencies to assess facilities and interact with young people.The move assumes significance against the backdrop of the recent student protests and the growing political importance of Gen Z and Gen Alpha.At the state level, similar pressure is visible.After protests at Uttar Pradesh's Sarvodaya schools, the government moved towards a new policy framework, filling vacant teaching positions and establishing management committees. Officials said the state has 103 Sarvodaya schools, but the gap between sanctioned and regular teaching posts remains substantial.In Maharashtra, tribal students have continued protests over hostel conditions, allowances, reservation-related concerns, scholarships, medical facilities and administrative policies. The government has withdrawn or reconsidered some controversial decisions, but students have insisted that verbal assurances are not enough.One student representative put the new demand bluntly: “Govt reassured us, but we are looking for some concrete steps being taken. Until then, we will continue with our protest.”That sentence captures the new mood.Assurances are no longer necessarily enough.Students want orders, deadlines, appointments, written commitments and visible work on the ground.The most important change produced by the current wave may therefore not be one resignation, one road or one new teacher.It may be the creation of a new expectation.A schoolchild now knows that a complaint can be filmed.A student knows that an unanswered memorandum can become a protest.A protester knows that a local issue can attract national attention.An administrator knows that a broken toilet can become tomorrow's headline.And a government knows that young citizens are watching.Educationist and former Delhi University professor Prabhu Mohapatra sees the protests as evidence of a deeper failure to treat students as stakeholders.For years, he said, education was approached largely as a “top-down policy” exercise without “adequately taking students’ interests into account”.“The protests also reflect the decline in the priority given to education. The deterioration was visible not only in infrastructure but also in teacher availability and the quality of learning,” Mohapatra said.His larger point is crucial.A school is not merely a building.A teacher shortage is not merely a vacancy.A broken toilet is not merely an infrastructure statistic.Each becomes a question of whether a child believes the state has kept its promise.The current wave may ultimately prove less important for the number of protests it produces than for the behaviour it normalises.India's youngest citizens are learning that institutions can be questioned.They are learning that collective action can produce results.They are learning to use social media not only for entertainment but also as a tool for documentation, mobilisation and pressure.And they are learning that accountability is not an abstract constitutional principle.It can mean getting a teacher into a classroom tomorrow morning.The generation that grew up with smartphones is now discovering the power of the smartphone as a political instrument. The generation still in school is discovering something even more basic: That raising one's hand in class is not the only way to be heard.The larger test, however, will be whether governments respond before children have to take to the streets.If they do, the current protests may become a turning point in public education.If they do not, the protests could become the beginning of a much larger movement — one that connects examination reform, unemployment, public-school infrastructure, caste discrimination, disability rights, tribal welfare, campus safety and institutional accountability into a single generational demand.
Article Summary: In 2026, the anger travelled from Jantar Mantar to government schools, tribal hostels, residential campuses, recruitment centres and even roads outside district collectorates. While Gen Z students and job aspirants drove the high- voltage protests over examination irregularities and recruitment processes, schoolchildren have increasingly begun demanding something much more immediate: A teacher in their classroom.

Article Title: Kanpur aircraft crash: AAIB to probe training flight that killed trainee pilot, instructor
Article Text:
A twin-engine trainer aircraft crashed near Kanpur Civil Airport on Thursday afternoon





NEW DELHI: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) will investigate the crash of a twin-engine trainer aircraft near Kanpur that killed a trainee pilot and an instructor on Thursday afternoon, the civil aviation ministry said.According to preliminary information, the Tecnam P2006T twin-engine aircraft, bearing registration VT-NBV, crashed around five nautical miles from Kanpur Civil Airport near Ganga Barrage on Thursday afternoon.The aircraft was operated by Garg Aviation Ltd, Kanpur, PTI reported."The aircraft was on a training flight in the Local Flying Area of Kanpur civil airport. There were two persons on board, a trainee pilot and an instructor. Both sustained fatal injuries in the accident," the ministry said in a statement.A team of three officials from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) will visit the crash site for regulatory oversight and coordination."The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has been informed and will undertake a detailed investigation into the accident in accordance with the applicable rules. The circumstances and cause of the accident will be determined through the investigation," the statement said.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) will investigate the crash of a twin-engine trainer aircraft near Kanpur. The aircraft was on a training flight in the Local Flying Area of Kanpur civil airport. There were two persons on board, a trainee pilot and an instructor.

Article Title: Pool of blood, cries for help, gym trainer on the run: How horror unfolded at Delhi model's home
Article Text:
A 21-year-old student named Muskan was fatally stabbed inside her Delhi home.





NEW DELHI: A 21-year-old student and model, identified as Muskan, was allegedly stabbed to death inside her second-floor home in west Delhi’s Tilak Nagar on Wednesday evening, with police suspecting the involvement of her former gym trainer, Imran.Muskan was reportedly alone at home when Imran allegedly entered the house, attacked her multiple times with a knife and fled. Hearing her cries for help, neighbours rushed to the residence and found her seriously injured and lying in a pool of blood.She was taken to a hospital, where doctors declared her dead on arrival.Police received a PCR call about the incident and have launched a search for the accused. “We are searching for the culprit,” Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Abhishek Gupta told reporters, adding that CCTV footage from the surrounding area was being examined.A senior police officer said, “A woman, around 21 years of age, was stabbed to death when she was alone at her residence. CCTV footage is being examined and police investigation is under way.”The police have formed multiple teams to trace Imran and are also scanning Muskan’s phone for possible leads. Investigators have raided the gym where Imran worked and his home, besides questioning his family members and friends.Police said Muskan and Imran had known each other for around one-and-a-half years. Some relatives and neighbours told investigators that Imran was frequently seen in the locality and had allegedly been pursuing Muskan, who was suspected to have rejected him.Muskan’s friend Aman said she was the youngest of three sisters. One of her elder sisters, who is currently in Chandigarh, allegedly called him after learning about the attack and asked him to rush to Muskan’s home.“I received a call, but I don't remember the exact time. They told me they were not at home and that someone had entered the house and stabbed Muskan,” Aman said.He said he immediately contacted another friend and asked him to reach the house and ensure Muskan received medical attention. By the time he arrived, an ambulance had reached the spot and taken her to hospital.Aman also alleged that Muskan’s sisters had earlier raised concerns about Imran allegedly harassing her.“He had troubled her earlier as well, and after this incident, suspicion immediately fell on him,” Aman said.The gym where Imran had worked also came under police scrutiny. Dimpal, a receptionist at Seven Zone Fitness Destination, said Imran had left the job around one to two months ago after complaints about his conduct.“His way of talking was not appropriate, and after that, he was fired. It has been 1–2 months since he left the job. There was nothing between them here. Yes, he tried to talk to her once or twice, but he was told to stop, and then everything was fine,” Dimpal said.The murder has triggered tension in the locality as Muskan and the accused belong to different faiths. Heavy police deployment has been put in place to prevent any untoward incident.Muskan’s body has been preserved at a mortuary and will undergo a postmortem on Thursday morning. Police are continuing their investigation and efforts are underway to arrest Imran.
Article Summary: Muskan was reportedly alone at home when Imran allegedly entered the house, attacked her multiple times with a knife and fled. Police have formed multiple teams to trace Imran and are scanning Muskan’s phone for possible leads. Investigators have raided the gym where Imran worked and his home, besides questioning his family members and friends.
